claims.statement: Both agent libraries expose the same runtime Settings model, read once at startup from the SANDMAN_* environment: Python `sandman_agent.config.Settings` (frozen dataclass with `from_env(env=None)` defaulting to `os.environ`) and Java `edu…agent.Settings` (record with `fromEnv()`/`fromEnv(Map)`), each raising `ConfigError`/`Settings.ConfigException`. Fields are service_name/serviceName, contracts_dir/contractsDir, llm_base_url, llm_key, llm_local_key, llm_models_file, kg_uri/kg_user/kg_password, nats_url, service_token, service_verify, plugin_inbound_token, artifact_store, config_dir, log_file.

SANDMAN_SERVICE_NAME is the only variable whose absence makes `from_env()`/`fromEnv()` itself throw ("SANDMAN_SERVICE_NAME is required"); every other setting is loaded as None/null and checked later by the service via `require()`, so a partially configured environment fails at the service's own require call, not at Settings construction.

For the five secret settings (SANDMAN_LLM_KEY, SANDMAN_LLM_LOCAL_KEY, SANDMAN_KG_PASSWORD, SANDMAN_SERVICE_TOKEN, SANDMAN_PLUGIN_INBOUND_TOKEN), a `<NAME>_FILE` variable takes precedence: when present, the setting value is the file's content stripped of surrounding whitespace and the plain variable is ignored; only without a `*_FILE` variable does the plain variable apply. An unreadable `*_FILE` aborts Settings construction with a ConfigError/ConfigException naming the variable and path.

SANDMAN_SERVICE_VERIFY_FILE is always a file (no plain-variable form): both libraries parse it as a JSON map `{callerName: sha256(token)}` into `service_verify`/`serviceVerify`, defaulting to an empty map when unset, and fail Settings construction with a message naming the variable when the file is unreadable or malformed. The A2A/REST layers use this map to verify incoming callers.

`Settings.require(*names)` takes component names (not environment names), rejects unknown names immediately (ValueError/IllegalArgumentException), treats null, empty string and empty map as unset, and reports every missing setting in one message that translates each component to its SANDMAN_ environment name: `<service>: missing configuration SANDMAN_A, SANDMAN_B`. Both libraries produce the identical message format, so a misconfigured deployment fails once listing everything missing.

When SANDMAN_CONTRACTS_DIR is unset, the libraries default contracts_dir to the repository checkout: Python hard-codes `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5] / "contracts"`, while Java `Settings.defaultContractsDir()` searches upwards from the working directory for the first directory containing `contracts/common.schema.json` (fallback `Path.of("contracts")`). Containers bypass the default by copying `contracts/` to `/contracts` and setting `ENV SANDMAN_CONTRACTS_DIR=/contracts` in every service Dockerfile.

Java agents get Settings/Contracts/StatusTracker injected rather than constructing them: `A2aServer` in agent-lib-a2a provides `@DefaultBean @Singleton` producers calling `Settings.fromEnv()`, `Contracts(settings.contractsDir())` and `new StatusTracker(settings.serviceName())`, so an agent overrides a bean only when it needs non-default wiring. Java agents additionally load their Agent Card from MicroProfile property `sandman.agent-card` (env SANDMAN_AGENT_CARD), baked into the Dockerfiles as `/contracts/agent-cards/<agent>.json`.

Each service declares its own required settings at startup via require(): the orchestrator requires kg_uri, nats_url, service_token and config_dir; the extraction-agent requires kg_uri, nats_url and artifact_store; the query-service requires service_token always and kg_uri when no reader is injected; the Java agents require kgUri for the KgClient bean and natsUrl at first publish; the plugin stubs require plugin_inbound_token plus artifact_store (extract) or service_token (detect).

LLM access is gated per project policy: Java `LlmAccess.forPolicy(settings, llmPolicy)` first requires llmBaseUrl and llmModelsFile, then requires llmKey for cloud-allowed projects and uses llmLocalKey (raising PolicyException "local-only project but no local virtual key configured" if absent) for local-only projects; Python's `ModelSelector` mirrors the contract. The tlr-agent only builds LlmAccess for approaches with `usesLlm() == true`, so the enabled `stub-name-match` approach never resolves the key files.

The presence of plugin_inbound_token flips authentication from service-token mode to plugin mode: in Python `_authenticator` returns a constant-time comparison against the inbound token yielding caller "owner" when set, otherwise a TokenVerifier over service_verify; in Java `A2aServer.caller` checks the inbound token with MessageDigest.isEqual the same way. Hence the same Settings model serves both agents and plugins.

Settings never expose secrets through logging: Java's `Settings.toString()` is fixed to `Settings[serviceName=…]` ("never print secrets") and `LlmAccess.toString()` likewise omits the key; library tests assert the rendered string never contains key material.

config/ holds the operational YAML files, mounted read-only at /config with SANDMAN_CONFIG_DIR: extraction/plugins.yaml, inconsistency/plugins.yaml, orchestrator/rules.yaml, query/intents.yaml, query/plugins.yaml and tlr/approaches.yaml (plus the planned llm/models.yaml, referenced by compose but not committed in M0). Each file is loaded exactly once by its owning service, unlike contracts/ which is fixed per task.

config/extraction/plugins.yaml is loaded once by the extraction-agent's Service: the raw file's sha256 becomes `config_hash` (fed into run input keys and trace-link ids), `plugins[]` routes artifacts to the first plugin matching kind/format/glob (non-matching artifacts use the stub extractor), and `explicitReferences.patterns` supplies the regexes whose matches become explicit-reference trace links. Plugin calls use the configured tokenFile (the plugin's inbound token) and timeout (default 10m).

config/inconsistency/plugins.yaml is loaded at CDI startup by `DetectorRegistry.load`: `detectors` switches ServiceLoader-registered detectors on/off (an enabled-but-unknown id fails startup with ConfigException) and `plugins[]` registers plain-HTTP detector plugins (transport other than `http` fails startup with "http only"; an unreadable tokenFile fails startup). Each plugin's inbound token is read from its tokenFile and its timeout defaults to 10m.

config/orchestrator/rules.yaml tunes only timing, concurrency, retries and TLR kind pairs — the event→step rules themselves are fixed in code (plan()/manual()). Keys are debounceSeconds, maxConcurrentPerAgent, timeouts per skill, poll.initial/poll.max, retry.maxAttempts/retry.backoff, and tlr.kindPairs (source/target artifact kinds plus the approaches passed to the tlr-agent). `Rules.load` parses durations like `30s`/`2m`/`1h` and merges timeouts over in-code defaults.

The orchestrator executor uses each rules.yaml knob at a defined place: debounceSeconds coalesces mergeable steps into one pending step, maxConcurrentPerAgent caps running steps per agent in tick(), timeouts[skill] (elapsed since attempt_at) triggers A2A cancel plus a retryable TIMEOUT failure, poll.initial/poll.max bound GetTask failure detection (completion comes from events), retry.maxAttempts/retry.backoff re-queue retryable failures while keeping the project lock, and kindPairs decide which changed×current artifact kinds get TLR steps (empty kindPairs skips TLR and routes unlinked changes to detection).

config/query/intents.yaml defines the M0 NL-query stub loaded once by the query-service's `Intents`: each entry has an id, a regex pattern that must fullmatch the normalized question (named groups become Cypher parameters) and a fixed Cypher template; every template must pass the Cypher guard at load time or startup fails. $projectId is bound by the service, never extracted from the question.

config/query/plugins.yaml grants plugin read access: `{plugin-id: [project, ...] | "*"}` loaded by `load_plugin_grants` at startup. A plugin principal's effective level in a project is viewer only when grants are "*" or the project is listed; an absent file yields an empty map and grants nothing, and local-only projects should be granted only to locally operated plugins.

config/tlr/approaches.yaml switches ServiceLoader-discovered trace-link approaches on/off with default params: `approaches.<id>.enabled` plus `params` (shallow-merged with per-request overrides via `Approaches.effective`). Only approaches listed with enabled:false are collected as disabledIds() and have their links deactivated at startup; approaches absent from the file (e.g. explicit-reference) are untouched.

Configuration is part of run provenance: the extraction-agent hashes the raw config file bytes into `config_hash` and feeds it into run input keys and trace-link ids, and the tlr-agent hashes the effective approach parameters (RFC 8785 canonicalized) as its configHash — so changing these YAML files invalidates run identity and prior results by design.

deploy/docker-compose.yml shares an `x-agent-env` anchor across extraction-agent, tlr-agent, inconsistency-agent, orchestrator and query-service: SANDMAN_LLM_BASE_URL=http://llm-replay:8000/openai, SANDMAN_LLM_MODELS_FILE=/config/llm/models.yaml, SANDMAN_KG_URI=bolt://memgraph:7687, SANDMAN_KG_USER from MEMGRAPH_USER (default sandman), SANDMAN_KG_PASSWORD_FILE=/run/secrets/memgraph_password, SANDMAN_NATS_URL=nats://nats:4222, SANDMAN_SERVICE_VERIFY_FILE=/run/secrets/svc_tokens_verify, SANDMAN_ARTIFACT_STORE=/artifacts, SANDMAN_CONFIG_DIR=/config, SANDMAN_LOG_FILE (default empty) and the OTEL_* pair. Each service merges it with its own SANDMAN_SERVICE_NAME, SANDMAN_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE and per-service extras.

Per-service environment beyond the anchor: orchestrator gets SANDMAN_STATE_DB=/data/orchestrator.db and SANDMAN_AGENTS as a name=url comma list of the three agents; query-service gets SANDMAN_USER_DB=/data/users.db, SANDMAN_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE, SANDMAN_SESSION_SECRET_FILE and the three owner URLs SANDMAN_EXTRACTION_URL/SANDMAN_INCONSISTENCY_URL/SANDMAN_ORCHESTRATOR_URL; the dashboard (profile dashboard) gets SANDMAN_TARGETS plus its own state DB, NATS monitor and gateway URLs; plugin-stubs (profile stubs) gets SANDMAN_PLUGIN_INBOUND_TOKEN_FILE and a read-only artifact store; llm-replay (not on the anchor) gets SANDMAN_LLM_MODE, SANDMAN_LLM_UPSTREAM and SANDMAN_LLM_RECORDS_DIR under the experiment.

Service build() factories read extra environment variables outside the Settings model, and the orchestrator/query-service entrypoints exit with the service name on ConfigError: orchestrator `build()` reads SANDMAN_STATE_DB (default /data/orchestrator.db) and SANDMAN_AGENTS; query-service `build()` reads SANDMAN_USER_DB, SANDMAN_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE (bootstrap admin created only on an empty user store, flagged must-change), SANDMAN_COOKIE_SECURE and the three owner URLs; the extraction-agent reads SANDMAN_MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES (default 1 GiB); llm-replay's own Settings.from_env reads SANDMAN_LLM_MODE (validated against live/record/replay), SANDMAN_LLM_UPSTREAM (required except in replay), SANDMAN_LLM_RECORDS_DIR and SANDMAN_VERSION.

The dashboard's SANDMAN_TARGETS is a name=url comma list of the six status-reporting services (the three agents, orchestrator, query-service, llm-replay), and the dashboard deliberately does not depend_on the agents ("it must show them when they are down") — the target list, not the dependency graph, defines the system overview. The dashboard image is planned for M1; its compose entry already defines the environment.

deploy/.env.example (copied to deploy/.env) holds only deployment-tunable values — MEMGRAPH_USER, SANDMAN_LLM_MODE (live/record/replay), SANDMAN_EXPERIMENT (LLM cassette directory name under data/llm-records), SANDMAN_LOG_FILE (default empty) and the OTEL_* pair — while all secret material lives in deploy/secrets/, generated by deploy/gen-secrets.sh which never overwrites existing files and regenerates svc_tokens_verify.json on every run with plugin entries under `plugin:<id>`.

Java agents resolve their YAML file with a MicroProfile override that falls back to the shared config dir: `sandman.tlr.approaches-file` and `sandman.inconsistency.plugins-file` (set by tests via application.properties); production resolves `tlr/approaches.yaml` or `inconsistency/plugins.yaml` under settings.configDir() when set, otherwise next to the contracts dir (contractsDir.resolveSibling("config")), so SANDMAN_CONFIG_DIR wins.

The inconsistency-agent reaches the query-service through MicroProfile property `sandman.query-service-url` (env SANDMAN_QUERY_SERVICE_URL, default http://query-service:8000) rather than through Settings, and passes it into DetectionService for triage-related status queries; its Notifications consumer additionally appends one JSON line per new/reopened finding to settings.logFile() when set.

Both Settings readers treat an empty-string environment variable as absent (Python `plain`/`env.get(name) or None`, Java `plain` returning null for null-or-empty), so compose's default-empty values like `SANDMAN_LOG_FILE: ${SANDMAN_LOG_FILE:-}` cleanly disable optional settings instead of producing empty paths; path-typed helpers skip Path construction for empty values.

Settings behavior is pinned by mirrored unit tests in both libraries: `test_units.py::test_settings_read_file_secrets_and_report_missing` (Python) and `LibraryTest.settingsReadFileSecretsAndReportMissingNames` (Java) both read a *_FILE secret stripped, parse the verify file into a map, assert the exact combined missing-configuration message ("tlr-agent: missing configuration SANDMAN_KG_URI, SANDMAN_NATS_URL"), reject unknown require() names, fail from_env on the missing service name and fail on an unreadable *_FILE path.

OpenTelemetry tracing is opt-in through standard SDK variables: Python `setup_logging` activates the OTLP exporter only when OTEL_SDK_DISABLED is set to "false" (default true), and compose passes OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT through from .env with the same default-disabled semantics — so a default deployment emits JSON logs to stdout (plus the optional file sink) without any tracing backend.
